newsitem.title: THAILAND: THAI STOCKS EDGE UP AT NOON IN LACKLUSTRE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: THAI STOCKS EDGE UP AT NOON IN LACKLUSTRE TRADE.

text.p: Thai stocks rallied marginally by midday on sluggish trade in the absence of buying incentives, a market holiday mood and the pending outcome of Thailand's economic reform package talks in Tokyo, brokers said on Monday.
"Very few transactions from my clients this morning. They may be sidelined or on vacation," said one broker at a local house.
Tuesday is a public holiday to observe Queen Sirikit's birthday. The composite SET index gained 0.95 points to 637 on 1.37 billion baht trade by the midday break. The SET-50 rose 0.23 to 48.40
Brokers said the market also waited for the outcome of Thailand's loans talks with the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya and potential foreign creditors gathered in Tokyo to hammer out an aid package of up to $15 billion to help shore up Thailand's ailing economy.
The meeting began at 0100 GMT and news conferences are scheduled later the same day.
Bangkok Bank rose two baht to 168 and Thai Farmers Bank fell one to 112.
